conclusion: Whatever this allele does, the two cohorts that tested it only see it at the oldest ages. Carriers were present at 60-79 and absent at 80-90 in the Iranian cohort, and under-represented among Finnish men of mean age 83. Neither result is significant. Nothing here is visible in midlife, so this row should not be read as a prediction for a younger person.
negatives: The same allele was non-significantly more common among robust (non-frail) participants, which is the opposite sign. If both halves were real this would be antagonistic pleiotropy; on present evidence it is more likely that neither is.
